# Local Gio changes

Base: gioui.org v0.10.2, copied from the project's installed dependency.
The root go.mod selects this copy; the shared Go module cache is unchanged.

- `app/internal/xkb/xkb_unix.go`: non-ASCII printable keysyms are converted through
  libxkbcommon to Unicode key names instead of being dropped. With Ctrl/Super,
  non-Latin alphabet keys resolve through a Latin group on the same physical key,
  falling back to XKB alphabet key names when no Latin group is configured.
  Text input/composition still uses the original symbol. This applies to both
  X11 and Wayland and also benefits Gio's built-in editors/selectables.
- `app/internal/xkb/shortcuts_test.go`: one focused test loads actual XKB maps for
  US/Russian/Ukrainian and Russian-only input, checks Ctrl+A/C and normal typing.
- `app/internal/xkb/xkb_unix.go` (`UpdateModifiers`), `app/os_wayland.go`: the layout
  Wayland tells (`wl_keyboard.modifiers`) is given to xkbcommon as the locked one
  only. It was given as the depressed, the latched and the locked at once, which
  xkbcommon adds up: with three layouts, every one but the first was the first.
  `TestWaylandLayoutGroups` types with three layouts.

- Transparent windows (`app.Transparent`, `app.BlurBehind`, `Config.Transparent`,
  `Config.BlurBehind`), for the messenger's photo viewer window:
  - `app/window.go`: a window whose driver reports `Config.Transparent` starts each
    frame transparent black instead of white, as js already did.
  - `app/os_wayland.go`, `app/os_wayland.c`: a transparent window sets no opaque
    region. With `BlurBehind`, a window binds `ext_background_effect_manager_v1`
    (wayland-protocols staging; KWin 6.7 replaced its own blur protocol with it)
    and sets a blur region the size of the surface, updated with the opaque
    region on every configure. `Config.BlurBehind` reports what the compositor
    granted, not what was asked. The effect object is destroyed before the surface.
  - `app/wayland_background_effect.{c,h}`: generated by wayland-scanner 1.22 from
    ext-background-effect-v1.xml, like the other protocol glue (see go:generate).
  - Every other driver copies Config fields by name and does not copy these, so
    elsewhere they read false and windows stay opaque. X11 would need a 32-bit
    visual and an EGL config chosen for it; Mesa's first configs with alpha use
    24-bit visuals. That touches `internal/egl`, shared with Android, and is left
    out. The Vulkan fallback keeps opaque composite alpha; Wayland uses EGL first.

- Hidden Wayland windows (`app/os_wayland.go`, `app/os_wayland.c`,
  `app/wayland_xdg_shell.{c,h}`): `xdg_wm_base` is bound at version 6 at most,
  instead of 1, so that the compositor reports a toplevel it no longer presents,
  minimized from its own title bar or task bar for one, in the `suspended`
  state. Upstream only knew of minimizing through `Perform`. The state
  of a toplevel configure becomes `Config.Suspended` with the xdg_surface
  configure that follows; resuming also ends `Minimized`. A suspended window
  acknowledges configures but draws nothing until it is shown again.
  The v4/v5 events `configure_bounds` and `wm_capabilities` get empty handlers,
  since libwayland calls a missing one through a null pointer. The glue was
  regenerated by wayland-scanner 1.22 from `stable/xdg-shell/xdg-shell.xml` of
  wayland-protocols 1.45 (interface version 7); the go:generate lines still name
  the system path. Compositors older than version 6 behave as before.

- Raising a window from outside it, as the messenger does from its tray icon:
  - `app/window.go`: `Window.Activate(token)` raises like `system.ActionRaise`,
    with an XDG activation token where the platform needs one.
  - `app/os_wayland.go`, `app/wayland_xdg_activation.{c,h}`: Wayland binds
    `xdg_activation_v1` and activates the surface with the token; without a
    token or the global nothing happens, as before (Wayland has no raise).
    The glue was generated like the xdg-shell one, from
    `staging/xdg-activation/xdg-activation-v1.xml` of wayland-protocols 1.45.
  - `app/os_x11.go`: `Run`, which runs on the caller's goroutine, flushes the
    X connection. Requests made from outside the event loop otherwise waited
    in Xlib's buffer until some other event woke the loop: a window raised
    from the tray stayed minimized, and `system.ActionClose` did not close a
    window until the pointer moved over it. `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW` carries
    source indication 2 (pager) instead of 0, which window managers treat as
    a legacy client.

- `app/os_windows.go`: once a window has been placed, `Configure` with options
  that change nothing but the title only sets the title. It used to place and
  show the window again from `config.Size`, which only `update` sets. The
  messenger changes its title often, and a window sometimes opened with a 0x0
  client area until maximized; this is the suspected cause, not a confirmed one.

- `app/window.go`: `Event` delivers the events a destroyed window left before
  creating a window again. A closing driver queues an invalid ViewEvent and
  then the DestroyEvent, but the DestroyEvent has already cleared the driver;
  the ViewEvent was delivered first, and the next `Event` call saw no driver
  and created a new window before the DestroyEvent came out. Every closed
  window thus left a ghost behind, with its display connection, XKB keymap and
  GPU context: about 290 KB of C heap per window on X11, found with glibc's
  mtrace, plus the driver memory. Every platform's driver queues the events in
  that order.

- `app/window.go`: a window that becomes suspended or minimized destroys its
  GPU context and draws nothing until it is shown again. In the messenger demo
  on Mesa, a minimized window then takes about 45 MB instead of 84 MB; shown,
  about 5 MB more. An earlier attempt was dropped because every restore seemed
  to leave 35 MB behind, but that was the ghost window above and glibc arenas
  never trimmed; with both fixed, six cycles stay flat.

- Blur layers (`paint.PushBlur`), for the messenger's floating message composer,
  which shows the chat history behind it blurred:
  - `internal/ops/ops.go`, `op/paint/paint.go`: the opacity layer op carries a
    blur radius (zero for `PushOpacity`); `DecodeOpacity` returns both.
  - `gpu/gpu.go`: a blur layer adds, where it is pushed, an operation filling the
    clip in effect there (a rounded rectangle, say). The layer is drawn to the
    layer atlas like an opacity layer, then halved in size a few times and grown
    back to half size, sampling with linear filtering, and that image fills the
    operation. This approximates a Gaussian blur with the existing blit shaders;
    no shaders were added. The atlas and the downsampled images use linear
    filtering, which composites 1:1 layers exactly as before. The downsampled
    images of a frame without blur layers are released. A render pass on an
    atlas page interrupted by a blur resumes with `LoadActionKeep`.
  - `gpu/gpu.go`: every step of the blur is exactly two to one from the layer's
    origin (an odd size reads a pixel past the edge, which the texture clamps),
    not a stretch by a fraction of a pixel. The size of a layer that changes
    each frame, as a menu's clip does while it opens, made the blurred image
    swim, and the text under the menu flicker. Test in the messenger:
    `TestBlurDoesNotSwimWithTheSizeOfItsClip`.
  - `gpu/gpu.go`: a full-screen opaque fill no longer drops earlier operations
    once there are layers, not only while one is open: layers index them.
  - `io/input/router.go`: operations inside a blur layer take no input and
    declare no semantics, since the layer repeats content drawn elsewhere.
  - Tests: `gpu/internal/rendertest` `TestBlur` (with `refs/TestBlur.png`),
    `io/input` `TestPointerBlurLayer`. `TestStrokedPathCoincidentControlPoint`,
    `TestPathReuse` and `TestStrokedRect` fail on llvmpipe with upstream v0.10.2
    as well.

- A new X11 window is set up completely before it is published
  (`app/os_x11.go`, `app/window.go`). `Run` runs on the caller's goroutine
  (see above), so `Window.Option` from another goroutine, such as setting a
  title while the window is still being made, reached `Configure` as soon as
  `SetDriver` had run. The atoms were still 0 then: `XSetTextProperty` went out
  with atom 0, and Xlib's default error handler ended the process with
  `BadAtom` in `X_ChangeProperty`, now and then at start. The initial
  `Configure(options)` also overwrote a title set meanwhile. `newX11Window` now
  sets the atoms, the keymap, maps the window and applies the initial options
  before `SetDriver`; `Window.init` applies options given while the driver was
  being made, as it does for actions.

- Emoji presentation in font selection (`text/gotext.go`): runs are split by
  face with an own copy of `shaping.SplitByFace`, which resolves a character
  followed by U+FE0F or the keycap mark U+20E3 to the emoji face (the one that
  has U+1F600) when that face has it, and keeps a combining mark in the face
  of what it combines with when that face has it. A character after the
  zero-width joiner U+200D is resolved the same way, for sequences such as
  🤵‍♀ that come without U+FE0F. `text/shaper.go`: `GlyphID.Notdef` tells
  the glyph drawn for a character no font has, so that the messenger can
  leave such emoji out of its picker. go-text picks faces rune by
  rune, so ©️, ↩️ or the keycaps #️⃣ and 1️⃣ were shaped from a text font,
  keycaps and sequences such as 🙂‍↔️ fell apart into wide runs of glyphs,
  and a one-line label cut them to "…". Test: `text` `TestEmojiPresentationFace`,
  skipped without a system emoji font.

- Color glyphs of the COLR table (`text/colr.go`, `text/gotext.go`): go-text
  returns a `font.GlyphColor` for them, which `Shape` and `Bitmaps` skipped,
  so that the emoji of Windows' Segoe UI Emoji were not drawn at all (Noto
  Color Emoji has bitmaps, and was). `Bitmaps` draws the layers of a COLR
  version 0 glyph, each an outline filled with a color of the font's first
  palette, once into an image at the glyph's size in pixels
  (`golang.org/x/image/vector`), kept in the bitmap cache, and shows it where
  `Shape` draws outlines. Layers in the color of the text go to `Shape`'s
  path. Tests: `text` `TestColorGlyphImage`, `TestColorGlyphBitmap`, skipped
  without a system font of such glyphs.

- COLR version 1 (`text/colrv1.go`): the tree of paints of a glyph
  (Noto-COLRv1, Fluent Emoji, the Segoe UI Emoji of Windows 11) is drawn on
  the CPU into the same image: outlines clip (`PaintGlyph`, nested ones
  intersect), solid colors and linear, radial and sweep gradients fill, as
  sources of `image/draw` that map a pixel back to the paint's font units,
  the transforms multiply into the matrix under them, and `PaintComposite`
  draws its two subtrees into layers and blends them: the Porter-Duff modes
  and the separable blend modes; hue, saturation, color and luminosity are
  drawn as source over. The image is as large as the glyph's clip box, or
  as the outlines of the tree. Variable paints are drawn as their default
  instance, the shaper setting no variation coordinates; the color of the
  text (palette entry 0xFFFF) is black in a paint. Tests: `text`
  `TestPaint…`, on outlines of their own, without a font.

- Emoji in bold, italic and monospace text (`text/gotext.go`
  `shaperImpl.ResolveFace`): fontscan prunes the fonts that stand in for a
  family to the query's aspect, all families at once, so an emoji font,
  which has one weight, is found only when the typeface names it (the theme
  names Noto Color Emoji, not Segoe UI Emoji), and nothing stands in for
  `monospace` with emoji. A character that the face found does not have is
  looked for again in the regular aspect with the `emoji` family added; the
  query is kept in `shaperImpl.query` to return to. Test: `text`
  `TestEmojiFaceInBoldAndMonospace`.

- Emoji as pictures (`text/emojiimages.go`, `WithEmojiImages`): an
  `EmojiImages` tells the emoji a text begins with and gives its picture at
  a size, as a set of sprites does. `shapeText` cuts such emoji out of the
  inputs before they are split by face, and lays each out as one glyph of a
  face that stands for the pictures among the shaper's: a square of 18/16
  of the text's size, 3/16 under the baseline, advancing 20/16 as the
  emoji of fonts do; the glyph's number is the picture's and one more, 0
  being the glyph of a missing character. `Bitmaps` draws the picture,
  asked for once at the glyph's size in pixels and kept in the bitmap
  cache. `EmojiPresentation` is exported for such a set to tell a lone ©
  or digit from an emoji the way the shaper does. Tests: `text`
  `TestEmojiImages…`.

- An emoji font of the program's own (`text/shaper.go` `WithEmojiFamily`,
  `text/gotext.go`): the family named draws, before the typeface's fonts,
  the characters that are emoji on their own and the emoji sequences.
  `emojiPresentation` tells the former: the supplementary planes'
  pictographs, the basic plane's Emoji_Presentation=Yes, and U+2600–27BF,
  which messengers draw as emoji whatever their presentation (Telegram sends
  a reaction's heart as a bare U+2764). Without the family they go to the
  query's emoji face, the one that has U+1F600, before a text font that has
  them in black. It is not one of the
  typeface's families: fontscan tries the families named before all that
  stand in for generic ones, so an emoji font named in the typeface would
  draw the digits, # and * of all text, which emoji fonts have for keycaps.
  Tests: `text` `TestEmojiFamily`, skipped without a second system font
  that has emoji, and `TestEmojiPresentation`.

Run the focused check from the project root:
`go test gioui.org/app/internal/xkb -run TestNonLatinShortcuts`.

- Pictures on the clipboard, for the messenger's message shots:
  `clipboard.WriteCmd{Type: "image/png"}` puts a PNG there instead of text.
  - `app/os_x11.go`: the window offers `TARGETS` and `image/png` while it owns
    a picture, and sends it for `image/png`; text targets are refused then.
    The PNG goes in one property: without INCR, a picture larger than the
    server's maximum request (BIG-REQUESTS makes it tens of megabytes) fails.
  - `app/os_wayland.go`: the data source offers `image/png` alone for a
    picture. It is written to the requestor's pipe in parts until all of it
    went, as a pipe takes only so much at once (text went in one write, which
    could be cut short too). The mime strings offered are freed.
  - `app/os_windows.go`, `app/internal/windows`: a picture goes on the
    clipboard in the registered "PNG" format, which keeps its alpha, and as a
    `CF_DIB` (`app/clipboard_image.go`, bottom-up BGRA) for other programs.
  - macOS, iOS, Android and js still take text only.
